environment: Humpback highway winds down: SEQ coast sees bumper season of whales and calves heading south
Great Barrier Reef gears up for its biggest night of the year as spring coral spawning approaches
science: Aussie marine scientists breed heat tough super coral to help the Reef ride out warmer seas
sports: Grand final fever and Spring Carnival buzz has Queensland sporting calendar firing on all cylinders
stories.overview: Full moon to trigger Great Barrier Reef mass coral spawning, nature's biggest underwater show

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, it's Friday the second of October and I'm Alex Mercer. We've got whales doing their last lap down the coast, coral getting ready to throw the biggest party of the year, and a grand final weekend that's got the whole state talking. And I'm Jamie, buckled in and ready to go. Honestly this is one of those weeks where good news just keeps turning up uninvited, like a mate who smells a barbecue three suburbs away. Love that for us. Let's get into it, starting with what's happening out on the water.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: First up, the humpback migration is winding down along the South East Queensland coast and what a season it's been. Whale watchers from the Gold Coast to Mooloolaba have been clocking record numbers of mums with calves cruising south back to Antarctica. It's basically the world's slowest, most majestic school run. Those little calves have put on serious weight in our warm bay waters before the big swim south, so good on us for being a decent nursery. Meanwhile up on the Great Barrier Reef, scientists reckon the spring full moon is about to trigger mass coral spawning, where entire reefs release their eggs and sperm into the water all at once. It is one of the great natural spectacles on the planet and it happens right in our backyard.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Sticking with the Reef, Aussie marine scientists have been busy breeding what they're calling super coral, strains that can handle warmer water a lot better than the usual stock. It is basically giving the Reef a bit of a gym membership before the heat of summer hits. I love that, tough coral for tough times. Researchers have been collecting spawn from naturally heat resistant colonies and growing them up in labs before planting them back out on damaged reef sections. It is slow, patient work, but it is exactly the kind of quiet science that doesn't make huge headlines yet could end up saving one of the most important ecosystems going. We will keep you posted as those super corals get out into the wild.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, good to be with you both. Spring is well and truly flexing its muscles across the South East today, with sunny skies for most of the morning before we see those classic afternoon buildups rolling in from the ranges. Expect top temps around the high twenties in Brisbane and Ipswich, a touch cooler on the coast thanks to a sea breeze kicking in after lunch, so if you're heading to the beach this weekend get there early. Keep an eye out for a few isolated storms developing inland later this afternoon, nothing severe, just the atmosphere reminding us that storm season is just around the corner. Back to you two.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Right, sport, and it is grand final season which means the state is split between couch coaches and backyard cricket getting a run before summer properly kicks off. Queensland clubs have had fans on the edge of their seats and local pubs have been absolutely rammed for the big games. And over at the track, Spring Racing Carnival is firing up at Eagle Farm and Doomben, with trainers and punters alike buzzing about the quality of this year's field. Even if you don't normally follow the gallops, there's something about a spring race day with a good hat that gets everyone involved. Can't go past a good hat, Jamie. Whether it's footy finals or the flat track, Queensland sport is proving once again it knows how to put on a show when spring rolls around.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: That's your ParkSyde Bright Side for Friday the second of October. Whales waving goodbye, coral about to put on a light show, and footy finals keeping the whole state entertained. It really has been a ripper of a week for good news around here. Makes you proud to call South East Queensland home, honestly. Couldn't agree more. Big thanks to Sam for keeping us dry and informed on the weather front today. And thank you all for tuning in, we love having you with us. Get outside this weekend and soak some of this spring sunshine up while it lasts. Too right. I'm Alex Mercer, that's Jamie, we'll catch you next time on ParkSyde Bright Side, stay bright and we'll see you then.
